Description: Why Join Ford of Mexico? Celebrating over 100 years of legacy in Mexico, we are more than just a business—we are a vibrant, collaborative community of over 14,000 innovators shaping the global future of transportation. At Ford, we build what matters, grow where it counts, and drive progress with heart. Whether you are collaborating at our state-of-the-art Global Technology and Business Center (GTBC) or manufacturing iconic, award-winning vehicles in our world-class plants, you will find a culture evolving together, built on trust, passion, and shared purpose. Here, your work moves people forward, and your growth is personal. Join us, and let’s build what’s next together. In this position... As a Vehicle Power Systems Modeling & Energy Optimization Intern within the Ford Champs Program, you will help advance vehicle electrical efficiency and energy management across our connected and electrified vehicle lineup. In this collaborative systems engineering role, you will analyze feature electrical loads, construct simulation models, and build digital traceability between functional requirements and physical power consumption, directly helping maximize battery life and elevate the ownership experience for millions of drivers. What You'll Do... Model and calculate electrical power consumption and energy budgets across diverse vehicle feature states, operating modes, and customer use cases. Establish and maintain end-to-end traceability linking functional engineering requirements, behavior-driven test scenarios (Gherkin), and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) architectures to empirical power data. Gather, structure, and analyze empirical electrical load data from physical vehicle testing, laboratory benches, and engineering repositories. Support the design of MBSE models (spanning requirements, structural hierarchy, behavioral states, and simulations) for low-voltage power distribution networks. Collaborate with Feature Systems Engineering, Controls, and Architecture teams to evaluate technical power specifications, assess supplier inputs, and conduct Design Failure Mode and Effects Analyses (DFMEA). Help standardize methodologies, automated templates, and simulation workflows for projecting vehicle power loads, reducing battery drain, and supporting cost optimization. You'll have... Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering (with controls/systems focus), or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Foundational understanding of vehicle electrical architectures, low-voltage power distribution, or embedded electronic systems. Analytical aptitude with experience organizing and interpreting complex engineering datasets using spreadsheet tools (e.g., Microsoft Excel) or scientific computing environments. Strong collaborative mindset with the ability to coordinate technical information across multidisciplinary engineering teams. Professional working proficiency in English (written and verbal), with the ability to clearly document engineering models, specifications, and technical reports. Even better, you may have... Academic or practical experience using scripting and numerical computing languages (such as Python or MATLAB/Simulink) for modeling and data analysis. Exposure to Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodologies and modeling tools (such as SysML, Cameo Systems Modeler / MagicDraw). Familiarity with automotive communication networks (e.g., CAN/LIN) and requirements management platforms (e.g., Jama, Jira). Ford of Mexico is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is essential to our success. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, or disability status. Our focus is to build the best team. If you think you can bring value to Ford, love to collaborate, prioritize and aim to deliver excellence in everything you do, we encourage you to apply! We thank all candidates for their interest, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted. #FordMexico

Title: Sr. Manager, Transportation Strategy & Analytics, Amazon Transportation Services Mexico
Description: Description This role plays a critical role in shaping Amazon's Middle Mile transportation strategy while delivering a best-in-class customer promise. This position balances multi-year network strategy with the analytical rigor required to direct a network that operates every day. This position is the single-threaded owner of Amazon's Middle Mile transportation strategy across Mexico, leading network design, transit time, analytics and procurement across multiple transportation products. This role owns how the network is designed, how fast we commit to be, what we pay for capacity and which programs we invest in, end to end from Fulfillment Centers and Sort Centers through to the final hand-off to Last Mile. The successful candidate will lead a diverse organization responsible for Cross-Network Transportation Strategy, Network Design and Capacity Planning, Transit Time and Delivery Estimate Accuracy (DEA), Network Analytics and Transportation Procurement, as well as the strategy layer of every transportation program in Middle Mile including Sub-Same-Day, Linehaul, Warehouse Transfers, Third Party Carrier (3PC), Partner Carrier Program (PCP) and Direct Injection, We-Pay, External Fulfillment, Vendor Returns (VRETs), Reusable Containers and 1P Fleet, plus future strategic initiatives. This role sets the plan; the Middle Mile operating organizations execute it. The role therefore partners closely with Transportation Operations, Sort Center Operations, Supply Chain, Last Mile, Finance, Procurement, Product, Tech, ACES and Global Transportation teams to build scalable transportation solutions supporting Amazon's long-term growth, and depends on influence and alignment rather than direct authority over execution. This leader combines strong business judgment, analytical rigor and executive communication skills to influence senior stakeholders, drive organizational alignment and define the long-term roadmap for Amazon's Middle Mile transportation network. Key job responsibilities Own the multi-year transportation strategy for Middle Mile Mexico, balancing Cost, Speed, Capacity and Customer Experience. Own the annual network plan and the quarterly capacity commit: node footprint, lane design, mode mix and 1P versus 3P. Own the transit time promise and DEA across the network, including methodology, targets and governance. Own transportation procurement: carrier sourcing, contracts, rate cards and cost per unit. Own the strategy and multi-year roadmap of every Middle Mile transportation program, handing each roadmap to the operating organizations to execute. Own the single source of truth for network speed and cost, including the scorecard and the KPIs leadership uses to judge the network: Cost per Unit, Transit Time, DEA, Capacity Utilization, Carrier Performance and Productivity (TU). Own OP1, OP2, headcount planning and investment proposals for transportation, in partnership with Finance. Build the mechanisms that keep strategy and execution aligned, and lead executive business reviews that land decisions with senior leadership. Title: Marketing Assistant
Description: About Manukora Manukora® is a global wellness brand, leading the fast-growing US Mānuka honey category. We're on a mission to preserve the power of Mānuka and deliver it to the world in pure, functional formats at uncompromising quality, purity and potency. Born in the wilds of New Zealand, we harvest one of the planet's rarest natural resources: raw Mānuka honey. This creamy caramel super honey contains unique antioxidants, prebiotics, and a special antibacterial compound called "MGO." Established in 2015, we are a founder-led, family-owned business headquartered in New Zealand with operations in the United States and globally. Manukora is a certified B Corporation, working with locally-based master beekeeping partners to produce the highest quality Mānuka, leading through ethical beekeeping practices and investing in our bees, their environment and the communities that surround them. We are a team of beekeepers, herbalists, food scientists, and wellness professionals working to deliver this one-of-a-kind honey and reimagine the immune and digestive wellness categories. The Role We're looking for a Marketing Assistant to help run consumer and product research at Manukora. That means our IHUTs (in-home usage tests), surveys, quant and qual studies, and research into new categories and competitors. Working closely with the marketing team. You’ll be deeply involved in the innovation side of the brand, and it's a really fun space to be in. You see products before anyone else does, hear straight from the people using them, and help decide what they become. No two days look the same. One day you'll be prepping product for a study, the next you'll be emailing participants, and the day after you'll be deep in survey results working out what they mean and what we should do based on data. You'll work closely with our operations, retention/CX, marketing and design teams on many projects. Presenting insights and suggestions is the exciting part, but it only works if the base is solid. A big part of this job is organizing, coordinating and checking details across teams. So two things need to be true of you: You're analytical. You can take messy data (survey results, customer reviews, retail data) and tell us what it means and what we should do about it. You're hands-on. You're happy building product kits, communicating with consumers, and designing marketing studies. What the Job Involves Running the logistics of our research: building product research kits, coordinating samples and shipping with our ops team, sending participant incentives, and checking every detail before anything goes out Designing studies and writing surveys Pulling together survey results, customer reviews, Amazon data, retail data and building dashboards Looking after the research inbox and other consumer-facing platforms Digging into new categories, from competitors' packaging to how consumers think and behave Turning what you find into a clear recommendation: what the data is telling us and what we should do about it Sharing reports with the wider team in a clear and concise format Helping improve our research systems and playbooks as we grow Helping out with a variety of marketing tasks across the marketing team Who You Are You're around 1–3 years into your career and already working in a professional environment. You want to build a career in marketing or consumer and product research You're analytical, you can piece the details together and go beyond the numbers You're proactive and heads on to new challenges You're creative and detail-oriented, you notice the small things and pay attention to what's happening in the market around you You're comfortable with data tools, you've used at least one BI tool (Power BI, Looker or similar), or you're very strong in Excel/Sheets, pivot tables included You communicate well across teams You're fluent in English, written and spoken. You don't need a background in marketing but are interested and looking for the next opportunity to learn and thrive in the space. Nice to have: any exposure to surveys, market research, e-commerce or CPG. Experience with Notion, Figma, Claude, Typeform. Why Join Manukora We're building the world's most loved functional honey brand — grounded in science, rooted in nature, and driven by purpose. You'll be part of a high-performing team who values honesty, impact, and balance. You'll get international professional experience working in a company born on a small island at the bottom of the world (New Zealand!). We move fast, work hard, and laugh often — and we're in serious growth mode.
